newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty drifts in quiet trade, depos above lombard.
newsitem.headline: Zloty drifts in quiet trade, depos above lombard.

text.p: Polish one-day rates jumped above the central bank's lombard rate of 25.0 percent as banks searched for cash to pay for T-bills bought on Monday amid low reserve accounts at the start of May reserve, dealers said.
They said banks were keen not to keep low reserve levels over the long weekend as it would multiply the negative balance. Thursday and Friday are market holidays in Poland.

"Banks entered the May reserve with low average reserve accounts which would get even worse over the long weekend. This, combined with T-bill payments, boosted rates above the lombard rate," said Adam Gadomski of Bank Handlowy SA.
At 0850 GMT overnight rates were at 24.00/25.50 percent against 10.00/18.00 yesterday. Tomorrow/next rates were at 23.85/25.20 percent against yesterday's 23.15/23.85 percent.
There is a net outflow of 581.5 million zlotys from the system today but a net of 445.4 million return on Friday.
"Rates are unlikely to fall back today," one dealer said.

On the forex market the zloty was killing time at the central bank established resistance of 2.5 percent from the parity rate and dealers said it was unlikely to find courage to go higher, knowing it would trigger an intervention. "Nothing major should happen with the zloty today," one dealer said.
At 0900 GMT the zloty was at 2.51/2.49 percent from the trading band centre against 2.52/2.47 percent at opening.
It was at 3.1582/87 against the dollar down from 3.1565/85 at opening and at 1.8293/98 against the mark up from 1.8305/15.
